reader_question_answers.question: What does “debt crisis” mean in this case, and what evidence supports that description?
reader_question_answers.answer: The story uses it as a framing for a persistent fiscal imbalance and large rising debt. It explicitly does not establish a market or political crisis. The charts support fiscal pressure, not an acute inability to borrow or a political crisis.
reader_question_answers.unanswered: The operational definition and timing of a crisis, yields, ratings and government instability.

reader_question_answers.question: How has France’s public debt changed over time?
reader_question_answers.answer: Gross debt rose from 59.7% of GDP at end-2000 to 119.0% in June 2026, about twice the share. Two increases of 18.6 and 16.7 percentage points account for 35.3 of the 59.3-point rise. The ratio fell from 114.9% in 2020 to 109.5% in 2023 but euro debt kept growing.
reader_question_answers.unanswered: None for the displayed gross debt trend; net-debt interpretation is outside the story.

reader_question_answers.question: What contributed to those changes?
reader_question_answers.answer: Annual deficits occurred in all 31 years from 1995 to 2025. Borrowing exceeded interest in every year since 2002. Old-age and health shares increased while interest and some other spending shares fell. These patterns identify fiscal contributions and offsets, not a full decomposition of debt-ratio changes.
reader_question_answers.unanswered: Quantitative roles of GDP growth, stock-flow adjustments, policy and demographics in long-term changes.

reader_question_answers.question: Why has the debt become a concern at this particular time?
reader_question_answers.answer: The debt ratio resumed rising after 2023 and interest reached 2.2% of GDP in 2025 after 1.3% in 2020, reducing the relief previously provided by falling interest costs. The story attributes rising interest to larger debt and higher rates since 2022.
reader_question_answers.unanswered: Why these changes amount to a crisis now; financing and political triggers are not supplied.

reader_question_answers.question: How does France’s situation compare with relevant historical periods or other countries?
reader_question_answers.answer: Compared with the 1990s, interest remains lower but debt is much larger; total spending share has changed relatively little. In 2025 France had higher revenue and spending shares and a wider deficit than Italy, Germany, Spain and the EU27 aggregate. Its deficit exceeded the aggregate in 26 of 31 years.
reader_question_answers.unanswered: Peer debt burdens and financing conditions are not shown. The reason for choosing these countries is not explained.

reader_question_answers.question: What consequences are already observable, and which remain uncertain?
reader_question_answers.answer: Accumulated gross debt and renewed interest pressure are observable; budget arithmetic leaves a continuing non-interest shortfall. The deficit also narrowed in 2025, which qualifies a uniformly worsening picture.
reader_question_answers.unanswered: Effects on services, taxes, households, beneficiaries, growth and political stability; future debt sustainability.

reader_question_answers.question: What can the supplied evidence establish, and what questions does it leave unanswered?
reader_question_answers.answer: It establishes pinned descriptive accounts, differences, persistent deficits, relative 2025 levels, changing spending shares, and source-attributed explanations for recent changes. It does not identify the long-term causal drivers or prove that France collects an appropriate amount of revenue.
reader_question_answers.unanswered: A full answer to why a crisis exists, why it occurs now, and the appropriate policy response.

reader_question_timing_limitation: Questions and verification materials were read in the same initial cat batch. These answers are separate from spontaneous notes but were written after outline/source/code exposure, not frozen before verification. Stage1/2 remain untouched.
custody_and_exposure: Original outline author-review references and author assertions were visible when the full permitted outline was read. I did not seek withheld review files or use their verdicts as independent evidence.
Build-code header mentions an approved outline revision. This is author context, not evidence of correctness or review.

Custodian supplied a correction: the doubled story H1 results from packet synthesis promoting frontmatter title alongside the original single body heading. I have not inspected the original; treat as supplied provenance correction and do not penalize writer for duplication.

corrections_separate_from_earlier_notes.correction: Packet artifact per custodian, not a duplicate original body heading. Earlier frozen observation remains as an accurate description of what was displayed.
CSV confirms nominal debt increased from 2663.9 to 3103.2 billion euros between end-2020 and end-2023 while the ratio fell 114.9% to 109.5%.
Archived INSEE text supports attribution to debt stock/rates, new revenue measures and slower inflation-linked spending. These remain attributed explanations, not a local causal estimate.

corrections_separate_from_earlier_notes.earlier_rendering_observations: Bottom text overlap on charts 3 and 4
corrections_separate_from_earlier_notes.correction: No reversal: retained. Numeric chart interpretation was recoverable, but annotation layout is crowded.

G1.scope: Pinned statistical measures and sources behind the four charts, descriptive central values and scoped INSEE recent-change attribution; documented reuse basis.
evidence: Dataset manifest pins URLs, retrieval dates, sizes and SHA256; offline build verified all eight archived inputs.
Independent JSON-stat checks matched all 7650 fiscal and 5760 functional CSV cells.
README/datapackage specify general government, gross debt, percentage-of-GDP denominators, annual versus quarterly vintages and overlapping functional classifications.
Archived Eurostat reuse page permits statistical reuse with acknowledgement; archived INSEE page documents Open Licence 2.0 and source/date requirements.
Archived annual article supports interest-stock/rate attribution, inflation/indexation and revenue-measure context.
G1.limits: Pass does not cover the unsupported adequacy-of-revenue judgment, acute crisis framing, a current online-source refresh, or a legal audit of every downstream reuse condition. D41GPAY cross-check described in README is not itself archived; archived INSEE wording does confirm exclusion of SIFIM correction.
G1.check_needed: Scope revenue claim to observed comparison; retain source/date attribution and review reuse conditions for any new downstream use.

G2.scope: Story section Not a shortage of revenue, particularly France does not collect too little.
evidence: A higher revenue share than selected peers demonstrates relative level, not sufficiency for commitments or the absence of a revenue contribution to deficits.
Independent calculations confirm principal numbers: 31 deficit years, 23 above 3%, 26 larger than EU; 2.9-point primary deficit in 2025; 36.36% interest offset of old-age-plus-health rise.
Most other areas shrank is supported for the selected mutually exclusive set: excluding old age and health, 9 of 16 categories fell.
G2.limits: The failed scope is an analytical overclaim, not fabricated data. Fiscal arithmetic and source-attributed mechanisms otherwise check out. Persistent deficits are not a complete debt-ratio decomposition; the story acknowledges GDP growth but could more clearly mention stock-flow adjustments.
G2.check_needed: Replace adequacy judgment with high revenue relative to selected peers; avoid implying borrowing alone completely explains debt/GDP changes.

G3.scope: Offline archived-input-to-CSV and supplied-chart-SVG reproduction in isolated scratch with existing supplied dependency cache.
evidence: Node v26.4.0 rebuilt all three CSVs and datapackage byte-identically.
All four generated SVG hashes match supplied expected hashes and anonymous stage3 SVGs.
Dataset validator returned zero errors and zero warnings.
Supplied corrupted-source-label rejection test passed 1/1.
All copied original inputs and original packet files remained unchanged.
G3.limits: This is not a reproduction of the webpage or SVG-to-PNG rasterizer. No dependency installation or network retrieval occurred. Cache contents were used, not independently reinstalled from lock integrity records. Dataset remains status archived; this review does not substitute for full adversarial parser certification.
G3.check_needed: For full presentation reproduction, supply the delivery renderer and its pinned configuration.

G4.scope: End-to-end delivered presentation renderer; inspected PNG charts and reproduced SVG geometry are a narrower checked scope.
evidence: All four delivered PNGs inspected twice in numeric order; observed values, scales and labels correspond to recomputed data.
Chart 1 uses zero-based ratio scale; chart 2 bars share zero baseline; chart 3 common-scale dots use an explicit 40–60 domain; chart 4 diverges around zero and uses a non-overlapping category set.
Bottom source/axis text collides in charts 3 and 4; units and time periods were still recoverable.
Supplied SVGs reproduce byte-for-byte, but rasterization code/settings and full page render were not supplied/verified.
G4.limits: No finding of materially false numeric visual encoding; overlap is a real delivered layout issue, not evidence that numbers are wrong. Reading-size/mobile/browser presentation remains unverified.
G4.check_needed: Separate bottom annotations from axis labels and inspect final rendering at intended reading size using the actual pinned delivery renderer.

interest.anchor: Specific consequential comparison revises an assumption.
interest.evidence: The combination of doubled debt and much lower interest than in the 1990s, followed by reversal, makes the fiscal-pressure puzzle concrete.
interest.limitation: Does not establish an acute crisis.

findings_depth.anchor: Computes relevant contrasts and unpacks the category carrying the argument.
findings_depth.evidence: Old-age +2.4 and health +2.0 contrasted with total +1.2; interest decline accounts for over a third of the combined increase; borrowing is compared with interest and peer deficits.
findings_depth.limitation: Not a quantitative debt-ratio causal decomposition.

argument_counterevidence.anchor: Clear answer but a material alternative or boundary remains omitted.
argument_counterevidence.evidence: Story acknowledges falling ratio despite rising debt, small total spending change, recent deficit improvement and lower historical interest; nevertheless higher peer-relative revenue is used to rule out too little revenue without establishing that proposition.
argument_counterevidence.limitation: A plausible adjacent 2 for descriptive fiscal sequence alone; lower rating reflects the central revenue judgment and limited crisis answer.

explanation.anchor: Defines pattern but leaves a central mechanism unclear.
explanation.evidence: Definitions and named INSEE attributions clarify stock/flow, ratio changes and recent interest pressure; mechanisms behind persistent deficits and crisis timing are not established.
explanation.limitation: For the narrower descriptive arithmetic section, 2 is plausible; causal restraint is a strength but does not answer the broader mechanism.

chart_design.anchor: Useful evidence but decoding/annotation requires effort.
chart_design.evidence: Comparisons and values are clear, but source notes collide with x-axis labels in charts 3 and 4; chart 4 needs the bottom text to recover interval and units.
chart_design.limitation: No mobile or full-page inspection. Core numeric reading remained possible.

writing.anchor: Understandable but a key implication/passage needs work.
writing.evidence: Plain numeric prose generally conveys the argument economically; France does not collect too little overstates the comparison, and Two steps up, none down requires the paragraph to qualify it.
writing.scope: Story text excluding synthetic duplicate heading.
writing.limitation: Adjacent 2 is plausible for most paragraphs. No penalty for custodian-confirmed packet title duplication.

reader_coverage.anchor: Main question partly answered, important follow-ups remain open.
reader_coverage.evidence: Debt path, persistent deficits, peer context and spending shifts are answered; crisis timing, observable consequences and why deficits persisted remain largely unanswered.
reader_coverage.scope: Commission and seven released reader questions.
reader_coverage.limitation: Several gaps require unavailable market/political data, which the prose explicitly acknowledges; in-reach revenue history and stock-flow caveats could still improve the answer.

outline_verification.finding: Final narrative follows the main outline sequence, but not all stated must-appear counterevidence is carried into prose.
evidence: The outline gives 1995-to-2025 revenue growth and equal 5.1% deficits; prose does not include those historical revenue numbers.
Outline notes Italy has a primary surplus and that debt change differs from deficit; prose omits those explicit counterpoints.
Chart plan calls interest bars; delivered chart and code use a line. This is implementation drift without a demonstrated numeric error.
Author statements about review and parser quality were treated as claims, not independent validations.

Pour respecter les critères européens de Maastricht, le déficit public doit être sous la barre des 3 % du produit intérieur brut (PIB). En 2024, en France, il dépasse ce seuil et s’élève à 5,8 % du PIB. Le déficit étant la différence entre les recettes et les dépenses publiques, pour le réduire, il faut donc baisser les dépenses et/ou augmenter les recettes.
